Breaking: AI Completes the Largest Mathematical Proof in Human History, Mathematician Bursts into Tears on the Spot | HTX InsightsHomeCrypto News监管政策Breaking: AI Completes the Lar...Breaking: AI Completes the Largest Mathematical Proof in Human History, Mathematician Bursts into Tears on the SpotmarsbitPublished on 2026-10-30Last updated on 2026-10-30AbstractThe Classification of Finite Simple Groups (CFSG), the largest mathematical proof in history, has been fully formalized and verified by AI. Spanning roughly 15,000 pages and developed by about 100 mathematicians over more than half a century, the "Enormous Theorem" provides a complete "periodic table" of all finite simple groups: cyclic groups of prime order, alternating groups, the 16 infinite families of Lie type groups, and 26 exceptional sporadic groups—the largest being the Monster Group. Because the proof was so vast and scattered, it was notoriously difficult for any human to verify in full, and errors were nearly inevitable.

The startup Axiom used a multi-agent AI system, AxiomProver, to translate the entire proof into Lean code. Starting on October 1, 2026, the system completed the task in just 24 days, producing a 43.1 million-line Lean codebase—now the largest open-source software project by line count, surpassing the Linux kernel, Chromium, Firefox, LLVM, GCC, and FFmpeg. Along the way, the AI flagged hundreds of anomalies, including 34 significant logical gaps. Most notably, it found a fatal flaw in John Walter's 1986 proof of the Unbalanced Group Theorem, providing the counterexample PSL2(49). Working with group theorists Richard Lyons and Ronald Solomon, the team devised a new route, and the AI itself proved a new result, "Preservation of simple tops," to patch the gap. Real-time news, insights, prices, trending stories, and expert analysis - all in one place.Europe’s largest asset manager Amundi tokenizes equity index fund on EthereumAmundi, Europe's largest asset manager, has launched a tokenized share class of its STOXX Europe 600 equity index fund on Ethereum, expanding its blockchain-based offerings beyond money market funds. The new share class was issued in collaboration with European asset-servicing company CACEIS, which provided the tokenization infrastructure, and will remain available through traditional investment channels as well. The fund tracks the STOXX Europe 600 Index, covering 600 large-, mid- and small-cap companies across developed European markets. Amundi said it plans to develop a broader range of tokenized funds for institutional clients and digital platforms, citing potential improvements in accessibility, settlement speed and operational efficiency. The launch follows the asset manager's first tokenized money market fund share class in November 2025, also developed with CACEIS on Ethereum. The move comes amid rapid growth in the global tokenized equities market, though the largest products remain concentrated in US-related assets. The value of tokenized stocks reached $4.24 billion as of Nov. 4, up nearly 27% over the past 30 days, according to RWA.xyz data, with the platform's 10 largest tokenized equity products all tied to US companies or US-listed securities, including Securitize, SpaceX, Circle and Alphabet. Meanwhile, European financial firms have pressed regulators to accelerate reforms; in April, a coalition of 39 companies and industry groups warned that the EU risked falling behind the US in tokenized finance, calling for expanded asset eligibility, higher volume limits and the removal of time restrictions on licenses under the bloc's Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) Pil

Just Now, Altman Reveals OpenAI's New Model: So Excited I Didn't Sleep for Two Nights | HTX InsightsHomeCrypto NewsJust Now, Altman Reveals OpenA...Just Now, Altman Reveals OpenAI's New Model: So Excited I Didn't Sleep for Two NightsmarsbitPublished on 2026-10-30Last updated on 2026-10-30AbstractOpenAI CEO Sam Altman revealed on a podcast that an unreleased internal model, tested during a weekend experiment codenamed "Hold-my-beer," solved decades-old unsolved academic problems across multiple disciplines—including the Navier-Stokes equations—astonishing researchers and keeping Altman awake for two nights. He described the moment as a collective shock and a turning point: the era of humans laboring for years on hard problems is ending, and even top mathematicians risk becoming obsolete, like farm horses replaced by tractors.

Altman warned that AI will uncover far more severe security vulnerabilities than expected, and that sandboxes may not contain a model far smarter than any human researcher—suggesting the internet itself may need to be rebuilt with AI. He advocated many slightly-superhuman agents working as coordinated "teams" rather than one all-powerful model, enabled by test-time compute and chain-of-thought, with millions of dollars of compute now able to attack a single problem in parallel.

He predicted a "Macintosh moment" for personal agents that eliminate "fake work" like filling out web forms, and argued companies' real moat will be fulfillment capability, not UI code. On recursive self-improvement, he said AI will soon design better AI architectures, capturing even 5% efficiency gains as major breakthroughs. The S&P 500 slipped 0.30% to 7,720.39, the Dow dipped 0.25% to 52,342.56, while the VIX rose 1.71% to 17.20. Small caps bucked the trend, with the Russell 2000 gaining 1.01%. Healthcare and real estate sectors rose 2.40% and 2.21% respectively, while info tech and communication services fell 1.18% and 1.87%.

Among megacaps, Meta rose 1.96% and Apple 1.48%, while Amazon fell 4.25% and Alphabet A dropped 12.64%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 1.42%, ending a four-day rally, with Intel down 3.62% and memory stocks broadly lower. The Nasdaq Golden Dragon China Index rose 0.20%.

Amazon reported Q3 net sales of $201.94 billion, up 12% but slightly below expectations, with EPS of $1.89. AWS revenue grew 39.3% to $45.98 billion, beating estimates, though online stores grew just 2%. Capital expenditures hit $77.26 billion, and trailing 12-month free cash flow turned negative at $42.36 billion. The company maintained its ~$220 billion capex plan and guided Q4 sales of $240-247 billion, sending shares down over 10% after hours.

Intel posted Q3 revenue of $16.5 billion, up 21%, with adjusted EPS of $0.52 beating estimates. However, Q4 guidance of $15-16 billion revenue and $0.25 EPS fell well short of expectations, sending shares down over 20% after hours. Data center and AI revenue jumped 78% to $7.3 billion, while client revenue fell 5%.
